newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast approves state oil palm asset sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast approves state oil palm asset sell-off.

text.p: Ivory Coast has approved sales of state oil palm industry assets to Ivorian and Belgian buyers as part of its privatisation programme, the government daily Fraternite Matin said on Friday.

Belgian buyers Societe Internationale de Plantations et de Finances (SIPEF) would buy part of the assets of state-owned Palmindustrie's Bolo, Soubre and Okouyo centre-west sites for 8.235 billion CFA, a statement from the presidency said.
After allowing for debt owed to the government, the net asset sale value would be equal to 2.150 billion CFA, it added. The statement was dated Thursday.

Private Ivorian buyers PALMCI would take a second tranche of Palmindustrie assets at Iboke, Blibouda and Neka southwestern sites for 12.873 billion CFA, or 12.339 billion CFA after allowing for debts.
Both sales meant 70 percent of assets would be sold, net of debts, with Ivory Coast retaining the rest, the statement said.
Debt repayment schedules for both are expected to be signed but no further details were available.
Ivory Coast has sold 35 of the 60 companies slated for privatisation under a donor-recommended plan due for completion by the end of 1997.
